articleTitle: Experimental investigation of EMP shielding effectiveness of reinforced-concrete cell model
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: For studying the EMP shielding effectiveness, various shielding cell models are established, which are composed with mesh of reinforcement bars or reinforced-concrete. The results of experiments show that if the reinforcement mesh cells and reinforced-concrete shielding cells are specially designed, shielding effectiveness for an EMP plane wave can be about 40 dB and 20 dB for E-field and H-field respectively.

articleTitle: Classification of PCB configurations from radiated EMI by using neural network
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: This paper presents a method of classifications of printed circuit board (PCB) with having several configuration by using neural network to recognized its spectrum. The learning process is accomplished by giving the neural network the different radiated emission spectra of 22 PCB configurations. The trained neural network is successfully able to predict the PCB configurations.

articleTitle: EMI resulting from a signal via transition through DC power bus-effectiveness of focal SMT decoupling
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Signal vias are commonly used in multilayer printed circuit board (PCB) design. For a signal via transitioning through the internal power and ground planes, the return current has to jump from one reference plane to another reference plane. The discontinuity of the return current at the via excites the power and ground planes, and results in power bus noise, and can produce an EMI problem as well. Numerical methods, such as finite-difference time-domain (FDTD), moment methods (MoM), and partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC), were employed herein to study this problem. The modeled results were supported by the measurements. In addition, the EMI mitigation approach of adding decoupling capacitors was investigated with the FDTD method.

articleTitle: Study on the elimination of surface wave by metal fences
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The microstrip antenna is a low-profile planar structure and is inexpensive compared with other types of antennas due to the ease of manufacture. However, patch-antenna designs have some limitations such as restricted bandwidth, low gain, and a decrease in radiation efficiency due to surface wave modes. Surface wave modes in microstrip substrates may cause the undesired energy losses and the reduction of the radiation efficiency of the patch antenna. A scheme to eliminate such modes by using metal fences is proposed. This structure can be easily realized by a metalated hole in manufacturing. It is observed that the patch antenna with this structure shows reduced levels of surface wave modes, thus improving the gain and the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation methods to assess EM terrorism effects
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: High power microwave (HPM) and ultra wide band (UWB) sources can represent a threat for the sensitive equipment of various military and civil targets. The paper focuses on effects on aircraft and discusses the modeling possibilities available today to estimate such a threat for modern airplanes. An evaluation of voltages at the input of electronics, based on measured attenuations of a HPM field in a cavity and induced voltages in the wiring of a car which can be considered as being similar to the structure of an airplane cabling, is presented. This estimation shows the potential danger for the electronics submitted to a low level HPM.

articleTitle: Power frequency magnetic fields of medium voltage switchgear. A concept for evaluating the field strengths under an exposure limit point of view
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Power frequency magnetic fields caused by medium voltage switchgear might disturb sensitive equipment such as video display units or might even conflict with exposure limits concerning people living or working near such installations. In order to prevent possible influences or adverse effects the knowledge of the magnetic field levels produced by the switchgear is necessary. A suitable concept to get magnetic field distributions around substations is described. This concept considers the emissions of switchgear from a general point of view and avoids investigating actual substations in detail. Rather it allows derivation of the field strength levels from the data of the switchgear type.

articleTitle: The threat of intentional electromagnetic interference
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: There is likely to be an increase in the number of incidents involving intentional EMI in the future. It is important that engineers be aware of the threat that it poses and that those who design critical applications where malicious damage would have serious consequences should start to consider this in their designs and the layout of their systems. Engineers need to be aware of the problem, assess the risks posed to their equipment or application and then take appropriate countermeasures.

articleTitle: The impact of deadtime effect on unwanted harmonics conducted emission of PWM inverters
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of unwanted harmonics spectra impacted by deadtime effect which is the one of the conducted emission sources at the load terminal of PWM inverters. The unwanted voltage from this impact is shown that it is depend upon not only load current direction, deadtime interval, DC link voltage but also amplitude and phasor of the load. The analysis with Fourier transform theory is clearly shown this phenomena and the simulated and measured results for harmonics injection PWM and discontinuous PWM with deadtime of 2% and 4% of switching time are presented in this paper. The deadtime compensated show the improvement for PWM inverter performance. The results show closed agreement between both of results with a good support from the analysis and simulation.

articleTitle: A mathematical model for ground voltage fluctuation in PCBs
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, the ground bounce (GB) effect in PCBs is characterized and presented in both the power/ground and the trace/ground configurations. A generalized 2-D transmission line equation (GTLE) model is used to solve the problems. Simulation results confirm that GB is induced as a result of the resonant behavior. In certain situations, GB gives rise to white noise in parts of the PCB structure.

articleTitle: Electrical properties and magnetic fields of a coaxial bus bar
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Instead of shielding disturbing busbars consisting of conductors with rectangular cross-section by wrapping them with high permeable material, the authors propose the use of busbars which are formed by coaxial tubes of circular cross-section. Due to their rotational symmetry, they do not generate a resulting magnetic field in their surroundings. In addition this specific form is endowed with some more advantageous qualities, e.g. low inductivity of the impedance matrix, little power loss, high mechanical stability in the case of short-circuit currents, and little influence of eddy current and proximity effect. They investigate the properties of an N-tube conductor system by solving a volume integral equation, where all interesting parameters can be calculated analytically. As numerical results for a three-phase busbar carrying arbitrary alternating currents, they display 3D-plots and diagrams showing how current density, power loss and voltage drops depend on frequency and geometrical relations. Furthermore, by comparing these results with those of a common bus bar which contains conductors of rectangular crosssection, the advantage of the coaxial busbar is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Space weather effects on technological systems on the ground
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Space weather refers to conditions in the Earth's near-space associated with particles and electromagnetic fields which may influence the operation of space-borne and ground-based technological systems. At the Earth's surface space weather manifests itself as geomagnetic storms and its effects are known as GIC (geomagnetically induced currents). Power grids and pipelines are systems experiencing GIC. In the former, transformers can be saturated leading to different problems, and in the latter problems associated with corrosion arise. GIC are driven by the geoelectric field induced by a magnetic storm. The complex image method (CIM) has been proved to be an efficient tool for calculating the geoelectric field. The basic principles of CIM are presented in this paper. Regarding the flow of GIC, a discretely earthed power system and a continuously earthed buried pipeline represent two extreme cases requiring different methods for determining GIC.

articleTitle: The test of electromagnetic field radiated by electrostatic discharge (ESD) from the real charged human body in the office
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A customised ultra-wide band E-field probe and H-field probe with wide band oscilloscope were used to test the electromagnetic field radiated from electrostatic discharge (ESD). Many tests were carried out by real charged human body discharge to the ground. The results show that the electric field in 10 cm by a human holding a metal pen with a potential of 2 kV discharge to ground is about 410 V/m and the magnetic field is about 28 A/m in the distance of 3 cm from the discharge. The band of the field is extremely wide, ranging from several MHz to above 1 GHz. The experiments also show that the amplitude of electric field radiated by ESD when a human holding a metal screwdriver discharging to the ground metal is many times larger than that of the human finger discharging directly to the ground. Electrostatic discharge is one of the most common harmful electromagnetic sources to electronic equipment in the office environment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility test for aircraft system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) test for an aircraft system has no available and official standards or regulations in China. In connection with EMC test for a certain aircraft and its electric subsystems, we put forward a test program for aircraft AC/DC power supply system characteristics, electromagnetic emission, electromagnetic susceptibility, and electromagnetic environment and antenna coupling. We not only determine the EMC safety margin of the aircraft system from a system viewpoint, but also evaluate the EMC performance of some key airborne equipment from an equipment viewpoint.

articleTitle: Full-waveform measuring system for lightning current caused by lightning strikes to tall structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In order to protect electronic devices against the effects of lightning strikes to tall structures, detailed information about the lightning currents are necessary. For this purpose, a full-waveform measuring system was set up on the north towers of Jiangyin Highway Bridge. In this paper, the calibration to this system is introduced and the results of simulating lightning currents are given.

articleTitle: EMC design techniques of large computing systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Large computing systems are the backbones of most large international corporations' computing power in all areas of critical applications; their reliability and availability without question are of utmost importance to all computer centers. The large systems due to their shear size pose a unique challenge to EMC designers in dealing with the spider-web-like network of system cables (antenna arrays) exposed to potential hostile EMC threats. In the paper the techniques and considerations going into EMC design of large computing systems are discussed.

articleTitle: The study of metal meshes on electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: There is a good shielding effectiveness of metal meshes on electromagnetic interference caused by all kinds of reasons. 11 metal meshes of different specification of four materials are tested at different frequency steady-state fields and single variable transient fields. Also, their shielding effectiveness is calculated and analyzed. The results of the tests and analysis show that: (1) shielding effectiveness is correlated with factors such as the meshes diameter, mesh variable-density structure standards and so on; (2) within a certain frequency, the effect of mesh size on shielding effectiveness is small; metal materials shielding effectiveness changes with the frequency's variety; and (3) in shielding of the tying measure of metal mesh weld show its superiority over the screw. We must ground the shielding body reliably. The tests and analysis results of this paper are of important significance in anti-interference study and application to electromagnetic compatibility, modern monitors, communication, and computer control rooms.

articleTitle: Full-wave analysis of the EMP induced current in cables near the ground
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FD-TD) method is applied to the analysis of the EMP induced cortical current in coaxial cables near the ground in this paper. This method is a kind of full-wave analysis method. Not only transmission line current but also aerial current is considered in the calculation of induced current. This method is used to analyze all kinds of cortical induced current. The result in this paper is reasonable compared to relative data.

articleTitle: A common-mode current measurement technique for EMI performance evaluation of PCB structures
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: An experimental technique that measures the common-mode current on a cable attached to a DUT for assessing EMI performance is introduced herein. The technique was applied to evaluate the EMI performance of a module-on-backplane configuration with different connectors and different connector pin-outs.

articleTitle: A method for analyzing and modeling electromagnetic radiation property due to common-mode current in clock strip on PCB
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The radiation from common-mode current of a clock strip is higher than other arranged strips on a printed circuit board (PCB). The electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of a PCB is affected seriously if the clock strip on the PCB is arranged unsuitably. Using electric dipole models, a method for analyzing and modeling the electromagnetic radiation of the common-mode current in a clock strip on PCB is presented in this paper. The theoretically recommended value to keep the shortest distance from a clock strip to other strips on PCB and the reference frequencies to think of the maximum radiation are given when a PCB is designed.

articleTitle: The evaluation of the electromagnetic emission from high-speed railway by pantograph and network parameters
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: This paper gives the curves of pantograph and network parameters vs. speed by calculation with perfected typical mathematical model first, then predicts the electromagnetic emission level of Jing-hu high-speed electric railway according to the interrelationship between the electromagnetic emission and the parameters of the pantographs and networks.

articleTitle: An experimental research on EMI filters capability in controlling EMP
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In an EMP filter there must be some suppressing components, such as TVS (transient voltage suppressor) or MOV (metal oxide varistor). They play a very important role in controlling transients into a certain level. On the other hand, both of TVS and MOV have their defects, such as the frangible overload capability, huge transient energy may cause EMP filters' failure. We have investigated some EMI filters. Initial results show that an improving EMI filter without suppressing components exhibits excellent capability in controlling EMP. Feed-through filters with larger capacitance can control very high EMP amplitude effectively.

articleTitle: A study on suppression of self resonance of metal chassis by means of the hybrid magnetic material
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Many noise suppression techniques have been applied and put to practical use, but in the near future, the signal processing speed and frequency spectrum will become increasingly higher, and the size of equipment will become smaller, and so new technology to reduce EMI radiation and to enhance immunity are still demanded. It is expected that not only the interference between inter-systems by EMI radiation from the equipment but also the interference inside the equipment causes the degradation of system reliability. The equipment cabinet constructed of conductive materials has self-resonance frequency. When electromagnetic excitation occurs inside the cabinet by EMI radiation from inner circuits, the strong electromagnetic field is generated inside the cabinet at the self-resonance frequency, makes EMI radiation from cabinet increase and degrades the immunity of the inner circuit. To suppress the radiation from the cabinet and interface cable by suppressing Q of the self-resonance and to enhance immunity are requested. The authors propose to use hybrid magnetic materials which contain magnetic material and dielectric material in order to suppress the value of Q and verify the effect.

articleTitle: Lighting overvoltage protection connected to low-voltage power distribution systems according to EMC
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The installation of SPDs (surge protective devices) in telecommunication plants is required according to the lighting protection zone (LPZ) concept, according to EMC, whenever an electrical line crosses the boundary between two zones. It determines the place for the installation of SPDs at the zone interfaces. In order to guarantee a safe protection of telecommunication systems, an energetic coordination method of SPDs among each other and between SPDs and the equipment to be protected is defined.

articleTitle: Using IDFT technique for antenna's time-domain near-field measurements
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: This paper described a new method which uses IDFT (inverse discrete Fourier transform) technique to perform time-domain near-field measurements for antenna. Some calculation examples show that this method is feasible and exact.

articleTitle: Suspended stripline and Ka band integrated mixer
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: An integrated planar mixer has been designed by using the home-made beam lead mixer diode. It is indicated by measurements that in the frequency range from 31 to 37 GHz, the frequency conversion loss of the mixer is 8.6/spl plusmn/1.4 dB and the local oscillation radio frequency isolation is greater than 19 dB.

articleTitle: Sources of electromagnetic disturbances in resistance welding inverter topologies and effective reduction techniques
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In the paper, existing possibilities to localize sources of disturbance within resistance welding inverter topologies are illustrated. Furthermore, the effects of the application of mains filters and noise suppression capacitors are also discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the field within bounded wave simulator with a large test object in the working volume
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A bounded wave simulator is an efficient broad bandwidth illuminator and has been widely used in simulating the EMP pulse propagating in free space with a plane wave model. A test object in the working volume will cause field distortion. In this paper, the FDTD method is used to calculate the field distributions when a test object is situated in the bounded wave simulator or in a radiated plane wave. The errors of the field distribution according to the different ratio of the test object dimensions to the height of the working space is calculated and compared with the field in free space, especially the tangential H field component on the conductor surface. The method to determine the maximum test size in an EMP simulator is corrected based on our discussion. The advantage of the new method is that the results are more reasonable than before.

articleTitle: Analysis of a thin-wire square-loop antenna using FDTD method
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, the input impedance of a thin-wire square-loop antenna with the different wire-radius is obtained using the FDTD method, where Gaussian type pulse and sinusoidal wave are used as the excitation source. The PML absorbing boundary condition and the infinitesimally small feeding gap have been applied to calculate the input impedance of a thin-wire square-loop antenna. The calculations of input impedance of thin-wire square-loop antenna are in good agreement with previous MoM results.

articleTitle: DC power bus modeling in high-speed digital designs including conductor and dielectric losses
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Power bus design is a critical aspect in high-speed digital circuit designs. A circuit extraction approach based on a mixed-potential integral equation formulation is presented herein to model arbitrary multilayer power bus structures including vertical discontinuities associated with surface mount (SMT) decoupling capacitor interconnects. Both conductor and dielectric losses are incorporated, and included into the first principles formulation. The agreement of modeling and measurements demonstrates its effectiveness and utilization in power bus designs.

articleTitle: An adaptive wavelet denoising method for the measuring system of EMP signals
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: An adaptive wavelet denoising method is proposed to eliminate the noise induced by the measuring system of EMP signals. This method employs a threshold-searching strategy to select an optimal denoising threshold for a given system. Wavelet decomposition and reconstruction are combined with neural network nonlinear threshold-filtering units in the new denoising algorithm. Based on a group of training signal, the denoising threshold can be learned adaptively. The training algorithm and application examples are given in this paper.

articleTitle: Development and application of LEMP-simulating device
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, a device is presented which is used to simulate a remote lightning electromagnetic environment. The device is composed of a set of surge generators and a set of parallel plate transverse electromagnetic wave cells (PPTCs). The field in the PPTCs is uniform so as to test the immunity of EUT. Experiments have been performed to testify its efficiency and feasibility. The results show that the device can work well.

articleTitle: Antenna factors of the new EUROTEM cell for fully compliant emission and immunity testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The EUROTEM(R) is a patented compact symmetrical TEM device with 4 striplines which are surrounded by a fully absorber-lined ferrite enclosure. Due to the broad band nature of the device, it is well suited for radiated emissions and immunity testing, compliant with the standards. In order to perform compliance measurements, the corresponding antenna factors have to be determined. Correlation to OATS measurements must be established. The EUROTEM devices are scaleable and can be built in different sizes. The range of test objects starts at printed circuit boards all the way up to two metre high racks. For large test objects, the arrangement can be fitted into an existing fully absorber-lined room. This arrangement is called EUROTEM-Antenna. By this retrofit, the conventional antenna mast and the typical EMC antennas are substituted with the EUROTEM antenna leading to savings in driving power and consequently in considerable cost savings for the amplifier. In contrast to the 10 year old GTEM technology, the EUROTEM is equipped with polarisation switching. The test object will be put on a turntable in the same manner as in any open area test site or absorber chamber. There is no rotation through the three spatial axes which is required using a GTEM cell and the corresponding manipulator. The EUROTEM is superior to the conventional technology by showing better field quality, better suppression of the non-TEM field components and in particular the better cost efficiency factor.

articleTitle: Comparison between some absorbing boundary conditions and numerical validation
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A comparison between some important ABCs in the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) technique has been made in this paper. These ABCs include Mur's second-order absorbing boundary condition, superabsorption technique and perfectly matched layer (PML) technique. Numerical tests are made. Some suggestions and conclusion are given.

articleTitle: Counterpoise in mobile radiotelephony
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The paper deals with the decrease of the radiation efficiency of hand-held devices due to energy losses in the operator's hand and mismatching of the device's antenna input impedance close to the operator's head. A set for model studies is presented. Comments to necessary modifications of protection standards are formulated. Some mysterious protection means are introduced.

articleTitle: Analysis of the earth potential problems of the electrified railway
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The traction return circuit of the electrified railway is usually that the overhead contact line system (OHL) transmits current to the electric locomotives, then the current returns to the traction substations by the rails and earth. That is, it belongs to the unbalanced power-supply system that uses the rails and earth as return conductor. Near the point of earth that current enters into the rails, it causes the earth potential to rise, and it cause dangerous impact or interference impact on the earthed telecommunication equipment and lines by the way of earth resistance coupling. Earth is assumed to be a homogeneous medium with an infinite plane in the existing theoretical calculation of earth potential. However, most of geology in nature where railway passes belongs to irregular nonhomogeneous medium. It raises a problem for theoretically calculating the earth potential. Furthermore, during the processes of survey and design of the electrified railway in the past, many technicians cited the earth resistivity that can be used for calculating mutual inductance coefficient to the formulas of earth potential. This method is wrong for calculating the earth potential in the nonhomogeneous medium. It may cause multiple error for calculating the earth potential and slip in adopting the protective measures for the earth potential. In view of the above-mentioned circumstances, this paper analyzes the characteristics of the interference sources and impact ways, and presents a new method for solving the problem of calculating the earth potential in the nonhomogeneous medium.

articleTitle: A novel simplified SVPWM control scheme for 3/spl Phi/ AC/DC Voltage-Source converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The paper presents implementation of a voltage source rectifier which based on a simplified space-vector control scheme. Calculation time is much reduced though the simplification of traditional space-vector-modulated algorithms. So a much higher switch frequency can be acquired to improve the line current character under the same hardware. Simulation and experiment results verified the accuracy of the control scheme, and which is simple to be implemented.

articleTitle: Development on waveguide cell for generating standard field
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, the development of the theory and a design scheme for a waveguide cell for generating a standard electromagnetic field are presented, The mathematical description of the electromagnetic field in a waveguide cell is improved. Should the impedance of each part of the waveguide cell system match well, the wave in the waveguide cell is a travelling wave. Thus, a quasi-uniform calibrating area can be established in the waveguide cell. The field strength of a certain point in the waveguide cell can be calculated with a theoretical uncertainty of less than /spl plusmn/0.5 dB.

articleTitle: Outage probability for microcellular mobile radio systems in Rician fading channels
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Rician models were used to analyze the desired signals' distributions. The effect of path loss lognormal shadowing and multipath fading was discussed. In this article, we utilized the outage probability to work over the influence to the desired signals which was caused by co-channel interference in microcellular mobile radio systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility characteristics of wireless LAN for indoor environment of buildings by FDTD method
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, the authors present the results of FDTD analysis of radio propagation channels, and the distribution of electric field intensities in several building structures are discussed. The results presented here are for the case of incident angle /spl alpha/=0/spl deg/. These results are useful for the design of the placement of the transmitter and receiver of wireless LANs.

articleTitle: Audio test in telecommunication equipment EMC performance
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this article, we discuss the audio or noise limits for telecommunication audio equipment and how to perform the test for it. Audio equipment always has some problems when it accepts a disturbance from outside, for example: there is noise when a telephone is disturbed by electromagnetic waves. So we must do audio evaluation in an immunity test. For the transient disturbance test, it is not easy to say which audio volume is suitable, because the noise or audio level will be very high during the EFT, surges, ESD etc. The audio evaluation is only performed in a continuous immunity test. In this article, we describe how to do audio test in RF electromagnetic field and RF common mode immunity test.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility analysis of GPS receiver
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Advanced digital GPS receiver antijam design techniques are stated, and a technique for interference monitoring and four interference mitigation techniques are described. The effects of interference are analyzed. GPS receiver tracking loop thresholds and tracking jitters are presented. The functional relation of jammer transmission power and it's effective range is presented. The jammer margin is defined.

articleTitle: Used FDTD method with PML and Mur ABC to calculate effective dielectric constant
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The absorbing boundary conditions (ABCs) are essential to terminate the computational space when the finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method is applied to analyze electromagnetic (EM) problems. In this paper, we used two kinds of ABCs to calculate effective dielectric constant of a microstrip. The comparison of these results has shown the advantage and disadvantage of these two ABCs.

articleTitle: Entire domain based diakoptic method of lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: An entire domain method of lines (EDMoL) is proposed here to take both the advantages of entire domain basis model and method of lines (MoL), which can save computation time significantly. This method is an extension of the triangular basis diakoptic MoL. The formulas of EDMoL are given in detail. Numerical examples and some interesting results are also presented.

articleTitle: Fictitious multi-medium method and its application in electromagnetic shielding calculations of underground telecommunication cables
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A fictitious multi-medium method is presented, where the conductivity or permeability of fictitious medium is negative. The discretization is confined to fictitious medium regions, so this method is requiring much less computer memories and timesaving. The validation of this method is verified by the electromagnetic shielding analysis of underground telecommunication cables.

articleTitle: Busbar transient current computation based on singularity expansion method
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In order to research the problem of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) in an electric power substation and the transient electromagnetic fields produced by the normal switching operations, the singularity expansion method (SEM) is used to compute the distributed currents on the busbar. Assuming the earth to be a perfectly conducting plane, the transient current under the unit step-function excitation is calculated. Because the basic parameters of the SEM depend only on the constructs parameters of the busbar, the SEM needs a few modifications as the excitation changes.

articleTitle: A response of series regulator to incident high frequency noise on AC-mains
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: It is important in order to guarantee the stable operation of a digital circuit to understand the response of a power supply to incident high frequency noise. In this paper, the response of a series regulator to incident high frequency noise on AC-mains is analytically and experimentally clarified. As a result, it is shown that high frequency response of a series regulator is influenced by the parasitic capacitance between base and collector terminals of the control transistor, the parasitic capacitance between negative-input and output terminals of operational amplifier, and the output impedance of operational amplifier.

articleTitle: Management of magnetic fields in large commercial buildings
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The magnetic environment in large commercial buildings is getting worse as the demand on power and energy is ever increasing. In this paper, technical approaches or measures for magnetic field management in large commercial buildings are discussed, which include rewiring, shielding and others.

articleTitle: Design of elliptic function LPF and its group delay equalizer [video signal processing]
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: This paper introduces a way of designing a low-pass filter (LPF) by an elliptic function. It then describes the design of a group delay equalizer to compensate the phase distortion present.

articleTitle: A new time-domain model of the impedance of lossy soil in MTL model
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In order to research the problems of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) at electric power substations or electromagnetic interference generated by carrier channels on multi-conductor power transmission lines, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and multi-conductor transmission lines (MTLs) model can be used. But the impedance due to lossy soil is dependent on the frequency, so the problem is very complex. One new model to deal with it in the time-domain is proposed using Pade's approximation. Contrasted with other methods, the model is accurate and can be used practically.

articleTitle: The CMA adaptive array for CDMA cellular communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The use of a constant modulus algorithm (CMA) adaptive antenna array at the base-station site to suppress interference and increase the user capacity of a CDMA cellular system is proposed. The improvement in performance is quantified by comparison with the omnidirectional antenna system using realistic simulation.

articleTitle: A study on a reduced crosstalk for the design of "CAT 6" high speed data transmission modular jack
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, a method of canceling and suppressing differential mode crosstalk noise signals caused by nonuniform coupling between two transmission lines in UTP (unshielded twisted pair) modular jacks is discussed. Differential mode crosstalk noise signals in balanced transmission lines in UTP modular jacks were suppressed by inserting auxiliary capacitances between balanced transmission line pairs which are closely located to each other. To verify the effectiveness of inserted capacitances, precisely calculated auxiliary capacitances were applied to 10 pin modular jacks which are used in a LAN (local area network) at 250 Mb/s with UTP cables. The NEXT (near end crosstalk) losses were measured to prove its applicability.

articleTitle: Spectrum consideration for wireless communications in the twenty first century
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: It is expected that wireless users will exceed one billion by the, year 2010. Besides voice, a new range of services such as multimedia, high-speed-data, etc. are being offered for delivery over wireless networks. Mobility will be seamless, realizing the concept of persons' being in contact anywhere, at anytime. There are some fundamental aspects such as limited spectrum, propagation effects, and unknown and time varying access will result in a profound impact on the choice of technologies to provide future mobile communications. So that the challenges to the technologies imposed by the radio spectrum limitations, radio channel propagation induced distortions, are seriously concerned by manufactures, operators, and regulators. The International Telecommunications Union (ITU) is engaged in development of global standards for wireless communications, and is referred to as International Mobile Telecommunications 2000 (IMT-2000). Wireless ATM (WATM) is expected to provide significantly high bit-rate services to meet the demand for handing multimedia information, such as high definition still pictures, moving pictures, and large files. In addition, WATM is required to provide a variety of services like CBR, VER, ABR, and UBR, and flexible connection, including symmetric/asymmetric bandwidth to support multimedia services. This article gives an overview of the frequency considerations of IMT-2000. It is very important in order to effectively use the limited spectrum resource and in selecting suitable third generation wireless technologies.

articleTitle: Study of lightning electromagnetic field distribution inside and outside the microwave communication building
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In the paper, the finite-difference expression is proposed to calculate the distribution of lightning electromagnetic field inside and outside the microwave station. The mathematical model is built and the initial condition and boundary condition are determined. The calculation method of variable step-size and data temporary storage increase by step is presented. It has solved the problem of abrupt change in medium, which is difficult to solve by an analytical method. The distribution and magnitude of the electromagnetic field inside and outside the microwave station are obtained. The calculation result of the electromagnetic field distribution in free space within the range of lightning stroke is close to the result calculated M.A. Uman.

articleTitle: Nonuniform potential distribution caused by lightning
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: One of the serious sources of electromagnetic interference is lightning. In modern intellectual faculties building, the electronic equipment system is very easily damaged by lightning. The calculation results show that the high frequency components of the potential difference along each floor in a building are quite different under a lightning strike on the building. It may cause the grounding potential to rise, damaging the electronic devices.

articleTitle: Solution of distributed capacitance of eccentric coaxial line by PMOBG method
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Mode analysis of TEM mode in a quasi-coaxial line is done by the perturbation method of boundary geometry (PMOBG), and its potential formula is presented. Moreover, the perturbation expression of the distributed capacitance of an eccentric coaxial line is obtained by the perturbation integral method, and its accuracy and applicability are discussed.

articleTitle: On integral computation of Bessel function for 3-D electromagnetic scattering computation in the earth half-space
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Using the integral equation method, the integral computation of the primary field of the 3-D electromagnetic scattering problem in the earth half space is an integral of double Bessel functions. The dipole model is usually taken for its numerical computation. The integral with integrand of double Bessel function is simplified to the integral of single Bessel function and is computed with the Hankel transformation. In this paper. A method of finding the zero points and dividing the intervals is used to compute the integral of double Bessel function. Taking different integral parameters, the integral results of double Bessel function are compared with those of single Bessel function with Hankel transformation. The errors of these two algorithms are discussed.

articleTitle: Surface impedance matrix boundary condition of coaxial cables braided layer
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The boundary condition of a coaxial cable's braided layer is discussed in this paper. Through introducing surface impedance matrix as the boundary condition, the contradiction with physical reality produced by using the boundary condition presented in other literature is solved. The new eigenvalue equation of the braided coaxial cable in free space and two corresponding modes are analyzed.

articleTitle: Scattering from apertures in an infinitive long conducting cylinder
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The specific case of loaded slot in a conducting circular cylinder is studied. This aperture is loaded by a parallel plate waveguide. The excitation applied in the problem is an electromagnetic plane wave incident perpendicularly on the cylinder. In the theoretical analysis, the authors introduce a directly solution with the moment method. After theoretical and numerical procedure, a general matrix equation is obtained by using the moment method.

articleTitle: Energy radiated by the switching of currents in a system of conductors
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The calculation of transient electromagnetic fields is becoming more important future because of the increasing demands on system design under EMC-constraints. The switching of currents in a system of conductors is especially crucial because a transient wave is stimulated in the nonconducting environment which can be responsible for the default of electronic systems. The total energy which is radiated by the transient wave can be calculated by integrating the Poynting vector over an appropriate closed surface and over the time interval between the switching moment and infinity. The calculation of the total energy radiated by a switching process can be simplified by applying the principle of conservation of energy. As a consequence only the energy which is dissipated in the conducting space during the transient current distribution after the moment of switching has to be calculated. The applicability is shown for two examples. In the first one a permeable and conducting hollow sphere is exposed to the transient field of a current of arbitrary time dependence flowing in a loop of arbitrary shape. In the second, a continuous current flowing in a homogeneous two wire loop in parallel with a solid conductor of rectangular cross section is switched off. At the moment of switching a part of the energy of the nonconducting space is transferred by a guided wave. The remaining energy can be calculated from the current sheet which is excited on the conductor's surface at the moment of switching. This part of the energy is dissipated in the material during the following transient current distribution.

articleTitle: Lightning overvoltage protection for financial computerizing systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Financial systems are nowadays dependent on electronic data processing technology. One of the most frequent causes of failure in this highly sensitive system are overvoltages mostly caused by lightning. This paper describes how lightning electromagnetic pulse intrudes into computer information systems and causes system damage. Damage prevention is also discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of the loaded network on electromagnetic scattering characteristic from slots
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Studying electromagnetic scattering from a plane conductor containing slots terminated by microwave network is of great importance to some practical problems. In this paper, based on the original work, the influences of the terminated microwave-network on electromagnetic scattering characteristic of slots are studied. We also pay attention to different practical application cases. Results are given. Almost for every case, there is special impedance with which the scattering field strength is the largest.

articleTitle: The consideration of some problems of lightning protection and earthing in telecom center
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In order to reduce or avoid human and installation damage by lightning, a lot of lightning protection and earthing techniques have been invented. The IEC publication 61024-1 'Structure against direct lightning' and China state standard GB 50057 'Design specification of lightning protection in structure' are the main guidance for structure against direct lightning in China. Due to the amount of precision equipment installed in a telecom center, carrying out these lightning protection standards, which aimed to protect humans and some basic installations only against lightning, is not perfect enough. It couldn't provide sufficient protection to the telecommunication network equipment. So the new effective measurements to protect the telecommunication centers and equipment against lightning need to be researched quickly. Though some specifications aimed at protecting telecom centers against lightning have been established, a lot of problems still exist. This paper provides some methods to solve the problems of direct lightning and lightning EMP protection, and earthing.

articleTitle: Calculation of normalized site attenuation from antenna factors
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, a site attenuation model in terms of the antenna factor of the transmit and receive antennas is presented. Both horizontal and vertical polarizations are included. Expressing site attenuation in terms of antenna factors allows the use of broad-band antennas with their attendant advantages over tunable dipoles.

articleTitle: The model of electromagnetic field through borders of different mediums
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference passes through different mediums and different borders to receivers in the form of electric field, magnetic field or electromagnetic field. Therefore, in order to compute interference surplus, especially the results of electric field, it is necessary to use specific border conditions. That is to say, using the given border conditions and natural border conditions can decide the constants in general outcomes of differential equations, then turning them into usable specific results. In the paper, rules of border conditions of vector fields can be induced through using the integrals of vector fields along a closed curve and closed curving surfaces.

articleTitle: Observations and analysis of the quasi-electrostatic field anomaly before the 6.2 earthquake in Zhangbei
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A Ms6.2 earthquake occurred at 11:50 on Jan. 10th 1998, the the strongest earthquake in China's Hebei province since the Tangshan Earthquake in 1976. Prior to the earthquake, the authors recorded obvious abnormal signals roughly at the same time from two observatory stations, one at the Handan Station in Hebei province, and the other at Sishui Station in Shandong province. The obtained materials can provide very good information on the study of the quasi-static field.

articleTitle: Test and study of impact of electrified railway on audio-video program production
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Through testing and analyzing the impact caused by the electrified railway on audio-video program production, this paper indicates that the electrified railway will cause obvious impact on the audio-video system, especially the audio frequency, within a certain distance. The interference is mainly electromagnetic radiation coupling interference. Under the condition of bad earthing, static induction impact will also become an interference source not to be ignored. The protective measures should be laid particular emphasis on increasing the balance level of the audio-frequency transmission line, improving the earthing effect or implementing the electromagnetic screening measures.

articleTitle: A comparison of interference cancellation and multiuser detection
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: We investigate the use of an antenna array at the receiver in FDMA/TDMA systems, to let several users share one communication channel within a cell. A decision feedback equalizer which simultaneously detects all incoming signals (multiuser detection) is compared to a set of decision feedback equalizers, each detecting one signal and rejecting the remaining as interference. We also introduce the existence of a zero-forcing solution to the equalization problem as an indicator of near-far resistance of different detector structures. Simulations indicate that multiuser detection in general provides better performance than interference cancellation.

articleTitle: Application of FD-TD method in calculating electric and magnetic fields in T-TEM cell
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FD-TD) method is applied to calculate the distribution of electric and magnetic field in Triple-TEM (T-TEM) cell that has been made in our EMC laboratory. A few important problems are studied carefully, such as: the simulation of wave source, the resistance plane and absorbing materials as terminal load at the back of the cell, the absorbing boundary conditions etc. The procedure for calculation is compiled in C++ language. The calculation results are analyzed carefully.

articleTitle: The evaluation for emission measurements above 1 GHz
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this article, we discuss how to evaluate a test chamber above 1 GHz and a limit line for measurements. We also give some advice how to do emission measurements in this field.

articleTitle: Power decoupling circuit for modeling and measurement of EMC characteristics of IC/LSI
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A circuit configuration is proposed which decouples an IC from the peripheral power source circuit. Merit is extended both on the standard measurement of the the EMI driving power and also on the low EMI circuit design of printed circuit boards. The two-stage decoupling circuit is found effective. These discussions are now conducted on a lumped circuit base, which should be further extended to distributed-parameter systems because the electromagnetic system is intrinsically distributed and the limit of the upper frequency to be considered is actually open referring to actual electronics applications.

articleTitle: The capacity increase of CDMA by the interference suppression for multibeam application
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: This paper presents a multibeam array to increase the capacity of mobile communications and to improve the QoS. Two attractive features, the suitable beam width and the appreciable increase of the capacity, are obtained for perfect and nonperfect beam control. The simulation shows that the cell can be covered by an arbitrary number of beams if the matching network is feasible. By the system-level simulation, the capacity is approximately proportional to the number of the beams in the single cell model.

articleTitle: A frequency spectrum model of the intermodulation products generated by paging transmitters
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The present paper presents a frequency spectrum model analytic method of the intermodulation products generated by paging transmitters. A frequency spectrum model and its simulation frequency spectrum of nineteen intermodulation products, which are generated by different kinds of paging transmitters, are shown. All these above could be used by the spectrum manager to identify the intermodulation interference. They could also be used to distinguish the interfering signals with the help of computer assisted software of searching interference.

articleTitle: Common-mode currents and radiation from PCBNGP
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper the closed-form expression for the common-mode current on printed circuit board with narrow ground plane (PCBNGP) is derived. The derivation is based on a three-conductor transmission line model. The common-mode and differential-mode resonances affecting common-mode currents and radiation are studied.

articleTitle: Automatic component immunity testing
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Schaffner EMC Ltd. has launched a series of test packages designed to test automotive components against the RF test specifications contained in ISO 11452 and SAE J1113. Each package is self-contained and complies with the highest test level specified in each standard. Significant cost savings can be made when testing to more than one standard as many of the items are common to all test packages. The article looks at the variety of RF test methods and parameters that are called up in the vehicle manufacturers' requirements, and shows how a test system can be put together using Schaffner's Profline 5000 systems to carry out just those tests that are needed, and to create reports in just the format asked for.

articleTitle: The implementation of a simple local matched load in FDTD computation of microstrip circuits
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A kind of simple local matched load (LML) derived from the concept of unsplit PML is presented and implemented in the FDTD computation of microstrip circuits. Since it is used below the metal strip of the microstrip locally, it is convenient to fit the complex circuits that have multi-branch structures. The difference equations in LML have the same form with those in the background medium, so it is easy to implement. Two examples are given to test the effectiveness of LML. The computation results are compared with the results simulated by MS-office software and those in from IEEE Trans. on MTT, vol38, no.7, p.849-56, 1990.

articleTitle: Shielding properties of infinite metallic plate with an aperture
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Shielding effectiveness and transmitted field distribution are calculated by using the finite-difference time-domain method (FDTD) and perfectly matched layer technique in this paper. An infinite metallic plate with an aperture illuminated by a steady sinusoidal plane wave is modeled. Some numerical results and discussions are given.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis of electric parameters of wire antennas in communication base stations
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid technique for combining the method of moments (MOM) with the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) is applied to analyze and compute the electric parameters of wire antennas placed in the communication base stations when considering the influence of the reflection of ground plane and the diffraction of surrounding objects. By means of this technique, an example is computed and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Wave mode coupling in lossy cut-off wave-guide
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper it is demonstrated that attenuation of transmitting wave is limited and the cut-off frequency is not distinct in cut-off wave-guide because of wave mode coupling. So it is advised to use metal material or plated layer with high conductivity when designing cut-off wave-guide or cut-off wave-guide filter with high performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of the emittivity of a chirally shielded cable
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The analysis of the emittivity of a chirally shielded cable is presented. An E-polarized cylindrical wave, coming from the centre of the cylinder, incides onto the chiral medium resetting in a coupling between TM/sup z/ and TE/sup z/ waves. The analytical expression of the shielding effectiveness in order to evaluate the emittivity has been derived and validated by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Design and experimental validations of a new shaped subreflector geometry for EMC oriented Cassegrain system
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A new shaped subreflector geometry for EMC oriented Cassegrain system is presented. The idea is to deform the classical hyperboloidal surface to reduce the spillover and the crosspolarization. The high gain antenna obtained can be used as a test antenna to detect external noises or to reduce the cross-polarization in a telecommunication system. Experimental validations resume the excellent results obtained for a 60 cm antenna/80 mm subreflector system in the 37-40 GHz frequency range. Different kind of antennas have been designed and now produced.

articleTitle: Buildings in high-speed mobile communication systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Wide-band digital indoor and future mobile communication systems are being developed in the quasi-millimeter and millimeter wave frequency bands. In such high-speed systems, the degradation of transmission quality by multipath fading constitutes a limiting barrier. Multipath fading, which results from reflection, refraction and scattering of radio waves by buildings and other structures, gives rise to more than one path reaching the receiver and produces a distorted version of the transmitted signal. In mobile and indoor communication systems it cannot be eliminated, therefore the multipath channel must be well characterized in order to reduce its effect in the design of such systems. The objective of this research is to study the multipath fading and delay spread effects due to buildings in an urban propagation channel. In particular, the effects of the building materials, shapes and number of buildings on multipath fading are being studied.

articleTitle: IEC standardisation of immunity to high power transient phenomena
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The objective of the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) is to produce civilian standards. This is of interest world-wide for the electronics and power industries in order to harmonise methods of protection and the development of protection devices. All information used and developed is unclassified. The intention of SC77C is to use existing IEC EMC standards wherever possible. Preparation of SC77C standards is consistent with the development of EMC standards and thus structured according to "IEC Publication 61000" which is divided into seven major parts. Only parts 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 are included at present. The present development of standards includes eleven active projects. This paper discusses progress of work on high altitude EMP on civil equipment and structures.

articleTitle: Computer-aided design of microstrip antenna array
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The design and manufacture of microstrip array antennas critically rely on computer-aided design (CAD) software tools. When the operating frequency is high, the full wave analysis is required. However, mutual coupling can be ignored for the majority of arrays. Therefore, the integrated analysis is not always necessary. In this paper, the full wave analysis is taken on the 2/spl times/2 subarray module and the loaded feed network separately. The CAD software tool is used in conjunction with the knowledge of basic array theory and physical insight of impedance matching through the Smith chart. An example of designing a Ku band compact microstrip array antenna is given to illustrate the above approach. The size in one dimension is reduced by a factor of 1.5 compared to the normal design. The experimental results agree with those of the theoretical prediction showing that there is no need for further experimental iteration.

articleTitle: Magnetic field reduction of power cables by multi-splitting of conductors and compensation effects
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The magnetic field of a twisted three-phase power cable of finite length can be drastically reduced by distributing its currents over 3N single conductors which are arranged in a specific order. The induction of the resulting multi-wire cable is expressed analytically by the help of integrals, and furthermore without integration by a simple model consisting of twist-free elements. As numerical results we display 3D-plots of the field distribution and diagrams of the resulting field attenuation factor for different splitting steps N of the original cable.

articleTitle: The study of lightning-protection grounding for power dispatching and communication equipment
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Because of irrational grounding, the normal work of dispatching and communication equipment is affected heavily, equipment can even be destroyed. The grounding problem for power dispatching and communication equipment in microwave buildings is analyzed in the paper. A comparison between separated and common grounding in different cases is made. An optimal grounding scheme is proposed according to the actual situation. This is of practical significance and theoretical study value for lightning-protection and anti-interference for specially sensitive automation equipment to the outside interference.

articleTitle: A method-of-moments approach to EM environment assessment nearby high-voltage transmission lines
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A moment method analysis is presented in this paper for computing the electrical field intensity in the surrounding space of a high-voltage multiconductor transmission line above the ground. In this analysis, the number of conductors, and the shape of cross-section of lines are assumed to be arbitrary. As a result, this formulation and its corresponding computer program would be applicable to the assessment of electromagnetic pollution produced by a high-voltage multiconductor transmission line system and may be used in calculation of interference between power system and telecommunication lines as well. The computed results are compared with those obtained by using an analytical approach and a good agreement between the two results justifies the correctness and effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Improvement on WKB solution of parallel polarized waves propagating in slowly varied dielectric
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: An improved Wentzel, Kramers and Brillouin (WKB) solution of parallel polarized waves propagating in slowly varied dielectric is given by the WKB method and perturbation techniques. The authors' result has hardly been restricted by propagation direction and its accuracy is shown to be better.

articleTitle: Investigation on the characteristics of the electromagnetic scattering near field from complex targets
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Calculation and analysis of the scattering near field from some simple and complex targets using a method of picture elements (PEL) and a computer program are discussed. The analysis is based upon a method of high-frequency approximation. The uniqueness of this method is derived from the simplicity of the theoretical basis such as the physical optics (PO) and the vector potential. The calculated results show that there are large differences between the near field and the far field. The characteristics of the near field are more complex. This work has practical engineering value in the area of the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), electromagnetic interference (EMI) prediction and electromagnetic scattering.

articleTitle: Common-mode currents in transmission line structures caused by asymmetric sources or load impedance
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: This paper describes decomposition using ideal structure extraction methods (ISEM) while asymmetric sources or load impedance is given, which makes the symmetric mode model (SMM) only contain differential-mode currents and the asymmetric mode model (AMM) only contain common-mode currents. With the assistance of the moment method, numeral computation of these typical structures gives valuable results.

articleTitle: Comparison of backscattering from cylinders with different cross section
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Shaping for targets is a main technology of radar cross section (RCS) reduction. In this paper the RCS of several different cross section cylinders are predicted, and the comparison between them is also presented. The conclusion from the comparison is helpful for very low observation designs, such as stealth aircraft.

articleTitle: A brief introduction of "technique regulation for protection of electro-static discharge"
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Electrostatic discharge is one of the most serious interference sources for electronic elements and devices. In the 21 century, the techniques of computer science, automatic control, telecommunication and micro electronics will group up very quickly. All these techniques are concentrated into a large building and/or individual workshop. For satisfying this situation, the Shanghai Construction Committee organized the interrelated institutes, companies and some experts to establish this regulation. It will be executed in the early 2000s. The essential contents of the regulation cover classification of the work environment for electrostatic protection, grounding technique, and material properties.

articleTitle: Radiation of wire buried in a lossy half space
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: A wire is buried in a lossy half-space. The finite-difference time domain (FDTD) is used to calculate the radiation pattern of the wire. One of the key technologies is near- to far-zone transformation proposed by K. Demarest, the other is contour integral model of a thin wire proposed by A. Taflove. The PML absorption boundary condition is used for truncation of FDTD lattices.

articleTitle: EM scattering by rectangular conducting flat plates with thin uniaxial anisotropic materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, according to the equivalence principles, high frequency approximation and boundary conditions, a method has been developed to deal with the EM scattering by a rectangular conducting flat plate coated with uniaxial anisotropic radar absorbing material (RAM). The simple but effective method is available to the system of RCS prediction in which the large complex targets are modeled by facets and wedges. Numerical results show some properties of EM scattering by conducting plate coated with thin uniaxial anisotropic RAM.

articleTitle: Representations of electric field between two inclined conductor boards
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The formulation E=U/d is traditionally used in the measurement of a GTEM cell, which is derived from two parallel boards capacitor. However, the basic structure of a GTEM cell is two inclined conductor boards. More accurate formulation is required and is mentioned in several papers. In this paper calculation formulation is deduced after investigating three models of inclined conductor boards and these results are compared with the result of the formulation E=U/d.

articleTitle: Electric field of asymmetric TEM cell
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: In this paper, the section of an asymmetric TEM was divided into four regions and potential function is expressed as a Fourier series in each region. The point-matching was used on the boundary of these regions to determine coefficients of series. Thus, the electric field can be calculated in terms of a potential function.

articleTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: Presents the front cover of the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Proceedings. Asia-Pacific Conference on Environmental Electromagnetics. CEEM'2000 (IEEE Cat. No.00EX402)
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.
